Ring was 7th in 2 hrs. 7 mins. 25 secs; Bert Mitchell 13th, 2 hrs. 14 mins. 16 secs.; and Fred White 23rd in 2hrs. 24 mins. Walker, Ring and Mitchell took second prizes in the team race.

Mick Walker was 3rd, Dick Towndrow was 4th, and Bert Mitchell 20th. The Red Cross "Ten" Race, held simultaneously with a 24-miles cycle race and 7-miles road walk, was a unique race, and a good crowd saw the three races start at the same moment.
Morrell was busy watching Tobin over a "pimple" who fought it out, eventually being joined by Bert Mitchell, who, after a while, made a great effort and drew away from them.

Joe Wilson, Bert Joels, Jack Tilling, Percy Reading, and Bert Mitchell (better known as a cross-country and marathon runner, also as a bee-keeper) made the grade both on the walk and on the grub-stakes.

Owing to the forward running of Dick Tobin 5, and Tom Clinton 7, our "B" team gained second awards, and our congratulations go to Charlie Smart and John Weames, who completed the "B" team. Tom Morrell and Fred Clay also ran well, as did Bert Mitchell, N.
Bert Mitchell and Tom Morrell completed our scoring six and we once again became the proud holders of the "Dewar" Shield, which is awarded to the winning club.
The Club teams have also done well in winning several 2 mile team races, also open medley relays, while Tom Clinton, Bert Mitchell and (whisper it) Bert Footer have done well in open road races.

Bill Lucas ran well to finish second with Ted Stimpson, now demobbed, in third place. Dick Tobin gained first-class standard, and Stan Eales, Norman Walker and Bert Mitchell qualified for second class by beating 16.30.
Syd Ring was third in 2.5.54, Bert Mitchell fifth in 2.8.10, Fred White seventh in 2.8.19, Gordon Doubleday eighth in 2.10.4, and Will Spencer eleventh in 2.17.21.
Bert Mitchell was the sixth scoring member of our team in nineteenth place, and our thanks go to Jimmy Wood, our second-claim member, for helping Bert along.
He also led our team to victory in the team race, our other men being Bert Mitchell 13th and George Chantler 14th, and the team scores were—Belgrave H. 31.
These two youngsters should be a great help to our teams for many seasons to come, and to beat such experienced runners as Tom Carter, Albert Frost and Bert Mitchell was a really grand performance.

George Chantler finished 6th but was running for our "B" team who were placed 4th while our "C" team finished 6th out of an entry of nine teams. On the 17th April in the Walton 10 miles race, Tom Clinton finished first with Tom Carter fifth, Geoff Pearson 14th and Bert Mitchell 16th.

Thirty runners, comprising seven teams finished the course and although our numbers were small, our lads all ran very well and we are sorry to hear that Bert Mitchell has been advised to give up distance running owing to leg trouble.

Frank Abberton, last year's winner, retired after 10 miles and Bert Mitchell also dropped out owing to leg trouble. Actual times and positions of our men were as follows: 13, Footer, 2 hrs. 55 mins. 46 secs.; 17, Ring, 2.58.48; 22, Smith, 3.3.4; 28, Chantler, 3.5.11; 39, Pearson, 3.10.40; 40, Porter…

I have not yet come across a 120 yards hurdles time—junior or senior—worthy of being accounted a Club record, and I should be glad to hear of a good hurdles performance. Bert Mitchell's Marathon time was over the measured Blackpool Corporation course. He finished 2nd, running for Ford Motors S.C.

BERT MITCHELL, always associated with our Club Marathon Championship Shield, paid us a visit on the occasion of the 20 Miles Open Run and promises that his next visit to Wimbledon will not be so long delayed.

The "Mitchell Trophy"is being awarded by the donor of this magnificent shield, Bert Mitchell of 32, Manor Road, Deal. Bert was formerly a fierce competitor and still remains a staunch Belgrave Harrier.
